pointers.sentence: Since 5.1 `LoginRequiredMiddleware` closes every view to an anonymous request unless the decorator `login_not_required` opens it (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:LoginRequiredMiddleware.process_view`).
5.0 added the functions `aauthenticate`, `aget_user`, `alogin`, `alogout` and `aupdate_session_auth_hash` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py`), with `HttpRequest.auser`.
`aauthenticate` awaits the backends' `BaseBackend.aauthenticate` in turn (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:aauthenticate`).

Since 5.2 `ModelBackend` and `RemoteUserBackend` have their own, on the asynchronous ORM, to "reduce context-switching", the 5.2 notes say (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend.aauthenticate`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

Since 5.2 `ModelBackend` and `RemoteUserBackend` have their own, on the asynchronous ORM, to "reduce context-switching", the 5.2 notes say (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend.aauthenticate`, `docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

`PermissionsMixin.ahas_perm` asks only the backends that have an `ahas_perm` (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:_auser_has_perm`; [Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](../auth/authenticating.md#aauthenticate-and-basebackend)).
The class can run either way, and so takes the mode of the layer inside it (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

Run asynchronously, `RemoteUserMiddleware.__call__` hands the request to `aprocess_request` alone; synchronously, to `process_request` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware.__call__`).
Since 6.1 `RemoteUserMiddleware.get_username` adds the prefix `"HTTP_"` only to the default header of an `ASGIRequest` (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware.get_username`).
Both now ask the user they are given for its session hash first (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`).
Since 6.1 `login` and `logout` replace `HttpRequest.auser` as they replace `user` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:_set_auth_user`).

`PBKDF2PasswordHasher`, first in the default `PASSWORD_HASHERS`, has had more iterations in every feature release since 5.0, 720,000 in 5.0 and 870,000 in 5.1 (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:PBKDF2PasswordHasher`).

But a right password checked against a string of an older count is hashed again and saved (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.check_password`; [Password hashing: `make_password` and the hashers](../auth/hashers.md#the-upgrade-at-a-login)).
CryptPasswordHasher went in 5.0, and SHA1PasswordHasher, UnsaltedSHA1PasswordHasher and UnsaltedMD5PasswordHasher in 5.1 (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`).
CryptPasswordHasher went in 5.0, and SHA1PasswordHasher, UnsaltedSHA1PasswordHasher and UnsaltedMD5PasswordHasher in 5.1 (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`, `docs/releases/5.1.txt`).
`get_hashers` imports every class of the list, so under all four releases a check raises `ImportError` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:get_hashers`).

With the name gone from `PASSWORD_HASHERS`, a string that hasher stored finds none, and `verify_password` answers it as a wrong password, without a warning (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:verify_password`).

It answers the opposite of `SessionBase.is_empty`: false for a store with no key and no data, without loading (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.__bool__`; [The session store: `SessionBase`](../auth/sessions.md#empty-is_empty-and-__bool)).
| `LogoutView` | Gone in 5.0: logging out by `"GET"`, which gets 405, through `logout_then_login` too | `django/contrib/auth/views.py:LogoutView` |
| `RemoteUserBackend.configure_user` | Since 5.0, always given its created argument, so an override without it raises `TypeError` | `django/contrib/auth/backends.py:RemoteUserBackend.authenticate` |
| make_random_password | Gone in 5.1, from `BaseUserManager` | `django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:BaseUserManager` |
| `ScryptPasswordHasher.parallelism` | Since 5.1, 5 where it was 1, "to follow OWASP recommendations", the notes say | `django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:ScryptPasswordHasher` |
| `AdminUserCreationForm` | New in 5.1.1: `UserAdmin.add_form`, which can save an unusable password | `django/contrib/auth/forms.py:SetUnusablePasswordMixin` |
| the validators' `get_error_message` | New in 5.2: each of Django's validators raises the message it returns | `django/contrib/auth/password_validation.py` |

| a model's default permissions | Since 6.1, follow a model renamed by a migration; under 6.0.8 the old rows stayed beside new ones | `django/contrib/auth/management/__init__.py:rename_permissions_after_model_rename` |
| `Permission.user_perm_str` | New in 6.1: the string `PermissionsMixin.has_perm` takes, such as `"journal.change_entry"` | `django/contrib/auth/models.py:Permission.user_perm_str` |
| the sessions' PickleSerializer | Gone in 5.0: with `SESSION_SERIALIZER` naming it, a store raises `ImportError` as it is made | `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.__init__` |

| the cached database store | Since 5.1, a failure of the cache on a save is logged to `"django.contrib.sessions"`, and the row's change stands; since 6.2, on a delete too | `django/contrib/sessions/backends/cached_db.py` |
| `MessagesTestMixin.assertMessages` | New in 5.0: checks a test response's messages against a list | `django/contrib/messages/test.py:MessagesTestMixin.assertMessages` |
